conclusion: No blocking correctness, allocator, continuation-ownership, or resource-limit finding in the external conditional-header layer.
review: Header frames, external request identifiers, and pending raw callbacks own their storage across user callbacks; parent suffix processing waits for child callback completion.
The child is an ordinary external DTD parser. Header lexical selection remains in the parent, including newly imported parameter declarations.

Shared read acknowledgment resets when an external request is delivered and initializes once per child after successful protocol encoding setup; nested skipped children can clear an outer read marker.
Active source and header parameter names are inherited in a distinct percent-prefixed namespace for recursion; active internal frames contribute to inherited depth.

Header bytes, replacement bytes, child construction, identifiers, and structural callback storage are charged before retaining or cloning them. Frame offsets advance and retained source/header scanning is bounded.

A missing header reference marks skipped declarations before a later child is created; DTD children inherit that state. The final mixed-header rerun confirms later imported declarations are suppressed.
limits: Malformed-input callback timing and detailed error locations remain incomplete, including existing entity-declaration byte positions.
Root NotStandalone callback order remains a separately documented difference.
Partial or errored child declaration state is merged only after successful finalization; the probe scope does not claim arbitrary incomplete child compatibility.
External PEs inside entity values and arbitrary declaration fragments remain outside this layer.
Twelve mixed-header cases retain missing sparse Default fragments for duplicate declarations in repeated external children; they preserve acceptance, error codes and declarations.
